_loader_notes: First-time guides for upper-body exercises. Same structure as content/exercise-guides/lower-body.json.
if_its_taken.swaps lists only genuinely similar exercises, and may be empty. The swap engine should use these lists instead of the catalogue alternatives.
Draft for coach review before launch.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Sit on the end of a flat bench with the dumbbells on your thighs.
Lie back, bringing the dumbbells to your chest as you go.
Feet flat on the floor.
form_cues: Press the dumbbells up over your chest until your arms are straight.
Lower slowly until they're level with your chest, elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Keep your shoulder blades gently squeezed together.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Elbows flared straight out to the sides. Tuck them in a little.
Bouncing the dumbbells off your chest.

if_its_taken.tip: No bench free? Do the same press lying on the floor, or use the chest press machine.

guides.where_to_find: Any mat space, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat.
Hold a dumbbell in each hand above your chest.
form_cues: Lower until your upper arms gently touch the floor.
Pause briefly.
Press back up.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Dropping your elbows onto the floor. Touch it softly.
Elbows flared wide.

if_its_taken.tip: You only need floor space and dumbbells, so you can do this almost anywhere.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Set the bench to a low incline, about two notches up.
Sit back with a dumbbell on each thigh and kick them up to your shoulders as you lie back.
form_cues: Press up and slightly towards each other.
Lower to the top of your chest.
Keep your feet planted and shoulder blades back.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper chest and the fronts of your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Bench set too steep, which turns it into a shoulder press.
Arching your lower back off the bench.

if_its_taken.tip: If no adjustable bench is free, a flat dumbbell bench press is the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: The flat bench stations in the barbell area, or a bench inside a squat rack with safety arms.
setup: Lie on the bench with your eyes under the bar.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Set the safety arms just below your chest height, or ask someone to spot you.
form_cues: Lift the bar off and hold it over your shoulders.
Lower it to your lower chest with control.
Press back up, keeping your feet planted and shoulder blades squeezed.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Benching heavy without a spotter or safety arms.
Bouncing the bar off your chest.

if_its_taken.tip: Benches go fast on Mondays. Dumbbell bench press is the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area: a seated machine with handles at chest height.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.
Sit with your back flat against the pad and feet on the floor.
form_cues: Press the handles forward until your arms are almost straight.
Return slowly until you feel a light stretch across your chest.
Keep your back against the pad.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Seat too high or low, so the handles are at your neck or stomach.
Letting the weight stack crash down between reps.

if_its_taken.tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area. Often the same machine as the reverse pec deck.
setup: Set the seat so the handles are at chest height.
Set the arms so they start just behind your body.
form_cues: Bring the handles together in a wide hugging motion.
Keep a soft bend in your elbows.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest.
common_mistakes: Bending your elbows a lot, which turns it into a press.
Letting the weight pull your arms too far back.

if_its_taken.tip: A dumbbell chest fly on a flat bench is the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Lie on a flat bench with light dumbbells held above your chest, palms facing each other.
form_cues: Open your arms out wide with a soft bend in the elbows.
Lower until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Bring them back together in a hugging motion.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy. Use lighter dumbbells than for pressing.
Lowering so far it strains your shoulders.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: Any bench, box or the bar in a Smith machine set at hip height.
setup: Place your hands on a bench, slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your feet back until your body is in a straight line.
form_cues: Lower your chest to the bench.
Keep your body straight from head to heels.
Push back up.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging. Squeeze your glutes.
Elbows flared wide.

if_its_taken.tip: Any sturdy surface works. The higher it is, the easier the push-up.

guides.where_to_find: Any mat space.
setup: Hands on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Body in a straight line on your toes, or on your knees to make it easier.
form_cues: Lower your chest towards the floor.
Elbows at about 45 degrees to your body.
Push back up, keeping your body straight.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Chest and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Hips sagging or piking up.
Only lowering halfway.

if_its_taken.tip: Doable anywhere there's floor space.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Set the bench upright, or one notch back from upright.
Sit with your back against it and kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height.
form_cues: Press the dumbbells up until your arms are straight overhead.
Lower to about ear height.
Keep your back against the pad and ribs down.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Shoulders and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Arching your lower back off the bench.
Lowering too far, past your ears, with heavy weights.

if_its_taken.tip: No upright bench free? Do the same press standing, or use the shoulder press machine.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart, a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height.
form_cues: Brace your stomach and squeeze your glutes.
Press the dumbbells overhead.
Lower with control to shoulder height.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Shoulders, with your core working to keep you steady.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to push the weight up.
Using your legs to bounce it up.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area: a seated machine with handles at shoulder height.
setup: Adjust the seat so the handles start at about shoulder height.
Sit with your back against the pad.
form_cues: Press the handles up until your arms are almost straight.
Lower slowly.
Keep your back against the pad.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Shoulders and the backs of your arms.
common_mistakes: Seat too low, so you start with your hands way below your shoulders.
Locking your elbows hard at the top.

if_its_taken.tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Stand tall with a light dumbbell in each hand by your sides.
form_cues: Raise your arms out to the sides until they're at shoulder height.
Lead with your elbows, with a slight bend.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The sides of your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and swinging. Light weights work best here.
Shrugging your shoulders up to your ears.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station: a tall frame with adjustable pulleys and a choice of handles.
setup: Set a pulley to the lowest position with a single handle.
Stand side-on and hold the handle with the hand furthest from the machine.
form_cues: Raise your arm out to the side up to shoulder height.
Lead with your elbow.
Lower slowly against the cable.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The side of your shoulder.
common_mistakes: Leaning away to lift higher.
Shrugging.

if_its_taken.tip: If the cables are busy, dumbbell lateral raises are the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Place one hand and the same-side knee on a flat bench.
Hold a dumbbell in the other hand, arm hanging straight down.
Back flat, like a table top.
form_cues: Pull the dumbbell up towards your hip.
Squeeze your shoulder blade back at the top.
Lower slowly until your arm is straight.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper back and the side of your back.
common_mistakes: Twisting your body to lift the weight.
Pulling towards your chest instead of your hip.

if_its_taken.tip: Rows are easy to swap: try a chest-supported row or the seated cable row.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Set a bench to a medium incline.
Lie face down on it with your chest on the pad and a dumbbell in each hand hanging down.
form_cues: Row both dumbbells up, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper back, between your shoulder blades.
common_mistakes: Lifting your chest off the pad.
Shrugging up instead of pulling back.

if_its_taken.tip: If no incline bench is free, do one-arm rows on a flat bench.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Hold a dumbbell in each hand.
Hinge forward at the hips, soft knees and a flat back, until your upper body is at about 45 degrees.
form_cues: Row both dumbbells towards your lower ribs.
Keep your back flat throughout.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper back and the sides of your back.
common_mistakes: Standing up taller as you row.
Rounding your back.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: Barbell area. Use a fixed barbell or a bar from the rack.
setup: Hold the bar with hands just wider than shoulder-width.
Hinge forward with soft knees and a flat back.
form_cues: Pull the bar to your lower ribs.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower under control.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper back and the sides of your back.
common_mistakes: Jerking the weight up with your hips.
Rounding your back.

if_its_taken.tip: If the barbells are busy, bent-over dumbbell rows are the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area or part of the cable station: a seat with thigh pads and a long bar above.
setup: Set the thigh pads so they hold your legs snugly.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width and sit down.
form_cues: Lean back very slightly and pull the bar to your upper chest.
Drive your elbows down towards your back pockets.
Let the bar rise slowly until your arms are straight.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The sides of your back, under your armpits.
common_mistakes: Pulling the bar behind your head.
Leaning far back and swinging.

if_its_taken.tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area: a tall machine with a knee pad or platform.
setup: Choose the assistance weight. More weight means more help.
Step or kneel onto the pad and grip the handles.
form_cues: Pull your chest up towards the handles.
Lead with your elbows.
Lower slowly until your arms are straight.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The sides of your back and your biceps.
common_mistakes: Dropping down quickly.
Only doing the top half of the movement.

if_its_taken.tip: The lat pulldown trains the same muscles and is the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station or a dedicated row machine with a footplate.
setup: Attach a close-grip handle.
Sit with your feet on the footplate and knees slightly bent.
Sit tall with your arms straight.
form_cues: Pull the handle to your belly button.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Let your arms straighten slowly without rounding forward.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Upper back, between your shoulder blades.
common_mistakes: Rocking backwards to pull the weight.
Shrugging your shoulders.

if_its_taken.tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station: a tall frame with adjustable pulleys and a choice of handles.
setup: Set a pulley to about chest height with a single handle.
Stand or kneel facing the machine and hold the handle with one hand.
form_cues: Let your shoulder reach forward.
Pull the handle back towards your ribs.
Keep your hips and chest facing forward.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The side of your back.
common_mistakes: Twisting your whole body.
Rushing the stretch at the front.

if_its_taken.tip: If the cables are busy, a one-arm dumbbell row trains the same muscles.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station: a tall frame with adjustable pulleys and a choice of handles.
setup: Set a pulley to about face height with a rope attachment.
Hold the ends of the rope with palms facing each other and step back.
form_cues: Pull the rope towards your eyes, separating your hands.
Finish with your elbows high and hands beside your ears.
Return slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The backs of your shoulders and upper back.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and leaning back.
Pulling to your chest instead of your face.

if_its_taken.tip: If the cables are busy, use the reverse pec deck or dumbbell reverse flys.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Hold light dumbbells and hinge forward with a flat back, or lie chest-down on an incline bench.
form_cues: Raise your arms out to the sides with a soft bend in your elbows.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The backs of your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Going too heavy and swinging.
Shrugging up.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: The resistance machine area. Usually the pec deck machine, used facing the pad.
setup: Sit facing the pad with your chest against it.
Set the handles so your arms start in front of you.
form_cues: Push the handles out and back in a wide arc.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together.
Return slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The backs of your shoulders.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and jerking.
Lifting your chest off the pad.

if_its_taken.tip: If it's busy, ask how many sets they have left. Gyms are used to people sharing.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing forward.
form_cues: Curl the dumbbells up towards your shoulders.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly all the way down.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The fronts of your upper arms.
common_mistakes: Swinging your body to lift the weight.
Elbows drifting forward.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: The dumbbell rack, usually along a mirrored wall in the free-weights area.
setup: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing your body.
form_cues: Curl the dumbbells up with your thumbs pointing up.
Keep your elbows by your sides.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: Fronts of your upper arms and your forearms.
common_mistakes: Swinging.
Only lowering halfway.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station: a tall frame with adjustable pulleys and a choice of handles.
setup: Set a pulley to the lowest position with a straight bar or rope.
Stand facing the machine, holding the attachment with palms up.
form_cues: Curl the handle up towards your chest.
Elbows stay by your sides.
Lower slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The fronts of your upper arms.
common_mistakes: Leaning back.
Elbows moving forward.

if_its_taken.tip: If the cables are busy, dumbbell curls are the closest swap.

guides.where_to_find: The cable station: a tall frame with adjustable pulleys and a choice of handles.
setup: Set a pulley to the highest position with a rope or straight bar.
Stand facing the machine with your elbows tucked by your sides.
form_cues: Push the handle down until your arms are straight.
Keep your elbows pinned to your sides.
Let it rise slowly to about chest height.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The backs of your upper arms.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring out or moving forward.
Leaning over the handle and using your body weight.

if_its_taken.tip: If the cables are busy, overhead dumbbell extensions or kickbacks work the same muscle.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Sit on an upright bench holding one dumbbell with both hands above your head.
form_cues: Lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows.
Keep your elbows pointing up.
Straighten your arms to lift it back up.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The backs of your upper arms.
common_mistakes: Elbows flaring wide.
Arching your back.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.

guides.where_to_find: An adjustable bench near the dumbbell rack, with dumbbells from the rack.
setup: Place one hand and knee on a bench, like a one-arm row.
Hold a light dumbbell with your upper arm tucked against your side.
form_cues: Straighten your arm back behind you.
Keep your upper arm still.
Bend back to the start slowly.
guides.where_you_should_feel_it: The back of your upper arm.
common_mistakes: Swinging the dumbbell.
Letting your upper arm drop.

if_its_taken.tip: Dumbbells are rarely all taken. If your pair is in use, grab the next weight up or down and adjust your reps.
